requirements.label: 128 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All College of Engineering BSE programs require 128 credit hours.

requirements.label: MATH 115: Calculus I
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 116: Calculus II
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: Linear algebra (MATH 214 or equivalent)
requirements.hint: CS-Eng requires linear algebra. MATH 214, 217, 417, or 419, or ROB 101 satisfies this per the CS-Eng program guide, and EECS 245 also counts per the official CS course lists.

requirements.label: MATH 215 or MATH 216
requirements.hint: CS-Eng requires one of MATH 215 (multivariable calculus) or MATH 216 (differential equations). If both are taken, the second can count as a flexible technical elective. MATH 205, 285, 286, or 316 can also satisfy this per the program guide, use the adjust control if that is your path.

requirements.label: Chemistry core
requirements.hint: Either CHEM 130 with the CHEM 125 and 126 labs, or CHEM 210 with the CHEM 211 lab for students who place into organic chemistry. Satisfactory AP chemistry credit also meets this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if that is your case.

requirements.label: CHEM 130 with labs 125 and 126
requirements.hint: General chemistry with both laboratory courses.

requirements.label: CHEM 210 and CHEM 211
requirements.hint: Organic chemistry path for students who place into CHEM 210. Placement here means no credit is given for CHEM 130.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 140: General Physics I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 160 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 141: Elementary Lab I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 161 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 240: General Physics II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 260 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 241: Elementary Lab II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 261 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: ENGR 100: Introduction to Engineering
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. Transfer students may substitute a course meeting the LSA first year writing requirement.

requirements.label: ENGR 101: Introduction to Computers and Programming
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. For CS-Eng, ENGR 151, EECS 183, ROB 102, or EECS 180 AP credit also satisfies this per the CS-Eng program guide.

requirements.label: Intellectual Breadth (16 credits)
requirements.hint: 16 credits of liberal arts courses, meaning courses marked HU or SS that are not also marked BS, NS, or QR. ECON 101 and 102 count by explicit exception. Up to 4 credits of approved professional development courses from other U-M schools may also count, use the adjust control to include those.

requirements.label: Humanities minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be humanities courses. Credit by test cannot be used for this minimum.

requirements.label: Upper level liberal arts minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be liberal arts courses at the 300 level or higher. One course may satisfy both this and the humanities minimum.

requirements.label: General electives (16 credits)
requirements.hint: Free elective credits that bring the program to 128 total. Any U-M course counts.

requirements.label: Residency (50 credits at U-M Ann Arbor)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. At least 50 credits must be U-M Ann Arbor coursework, including at least 30 credits of 300 level or higher technical courses offered by the College of Engineering in Ann Arbor.

requirements.label: EECS 203: Discrete Mathematics
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required. MATH 465 or MATH 565 also satisfy this per the CS-Eng program guide, though they require significantly more mathematical background.

requirements.label: EECS 280: Programming and Introductory Data Structures
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required.

requirements.label: EECS 281: Data Structures and Algorithms
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required. This is the gateway course to all upper level CS courses.

requirements.label: EECS 370: Introduction to Computer Organization
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required.

requirements.label: EECS 376: Foundations of Computer Science
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required.

requirements.label: EECS 496: Major Design Experience Professionalism (2 credits)
requirements.hint: 2 credits, C or better required. EECS 295 or an approved equivalent also satisfies this per the CS-Eng program guide.

requirements.label: TCHNCLCM 300: Technical Communication for CS
requirements.hint: Major core course, C or better required. Waived for students who take ROB 204 as a flexible technical elective, per the CS-Eng program guide.

requirements.label: Probability and Statistics
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of STATS 250, DATASCI 101, STATS 280, STATS 412, STATS 426, EECS 301, ECON 451, IOE 265, TO 301, or MATH or STATS 425, 525, or 526, C or better. Students with AP statistics credit should pursue STATS 280 for this requirement, per the CS-Eng program guide.

requirements.label: Capstone (MDE) Course
requirements.hint: One approved capstone course, C or better, recommended in one of your final two semesters. Approved: EECS 440, 441, 443 (senior thesis), 447 (begins Winter 2027), 448, 449, 467, 472 (replaces EECS 470 as capstone starting Winter 2026), 473, 480, 494, 495, 497, CSE 596, and AEROSP 388 (CS approved projects only). EECS 498 counts only in sections marked as capstone, and a course may count toward the capstone or the ULCS electives, not both.

requirements.label: TCHNCLCM 497: Technical Writing and Oral Presentation
requirements.hint: C or better required. Must be taken in the same or a later semester as the capstone course, preferably the same semester.

requirements.label: Upper Level CS (ULCS) Electives: 12 Credits
requirements.hint: At least 12 credits from the approved ULCS list, C or better per course. EECS 498 counts only in sections marked as ULCS, and EECS 404 begins Winter 2027. Per the CS course lists spreadsheet linked from the CS-Eng Program Guide, Fall 2025-Summer 2026.

requirements.label: 15 Total ULCS Elective Credits
requirements.hint: 15 total ULCS elective credits required, C or better per course. At least 12 credits must come from the ULCS list, the remaining 3 may come from the Expanded ULCS list: CSE 572, 574, 575, 577, EECS 444/ECE 544, EECS 453, 460, 461, 465/ROB 422, 553, and, beginning Winter 2026, any 500 level EECS or CSE course (the planner matches the 500 level courses in its catalog). Special topics EECS 498 and CSE 598 count only in sections marked as ULCS or Expanded ULCS.

requirements.label: Technical Electives: 25 Total Credits
requirements.hint: 25 total credits of technical electives, C or better per course, combining the 15 ULCS credits with up to 10 credits from the flexible technical elective lists. The planner matches courses named on the official CSE lists; many subjects also count at the 300 level or higher per the flexible list, use the adjust control for those. At most 4 credits of directed or independent study can count toward technical electives.
